title: 21 Best Trading Quotes and the Lesson Behind Each One
summary: 21 trading quotes from Buffett, Livermore, Paul Tudor Jones and Indian investors, traced to their sources, with what each one means for your trades.
body_markdown:
Trading quotes are short lines from experienced traders and investors that capture a lesson about risk, psychology or how markets behave. The most useful ones point to a rule you can apply, like cutting losses early or sizing positions so one bad trade can’t knock you out.


Below are 21 trading quotes from Warren Buffett, Paul Tudor Jones, Jesse Livermore, Rakesh Jhunjhunwala and others. We traced each one to its source and flagged two famous lines that usually carry the wrong name. We also turned every quote into a lesson you can test on[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/) .

## Trading Quotes on Risk Management


Almost every great trader starts with the same advice: protect your capital first.


### 1. “Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1.”


**Source:** This is Warren Buffett, as quoted in *The Tao of Warren Buffett* .


**Lesson:** Buffett doesn’t mean you will never have a losing trade. He means you should avoid losses so big they are hard to recover from. A 50% loss needs a 100% gain just to get back to where you started, so[size each position](https://algotest.in/blog/position-size-calculator/) with that maths in mind.


### 2. “The most important rule of trading is to play great defense, not great offense.”


**Source:** Paul Tudor Jones said this in his interview for Jack Schwager’s *Market Wizards* (1989).


**Lesson:** Jones decides where his stop will be before he enters a trade, so he always knows his worst case. Know your exit and your maximum loss before you place the order.


### 3. “The elements of good trading are cutting losses, cutting losses, and cutting losses.”


**Source:** Ed Seykota said this in *Market Wizards* . He was one of the first traders to manage client money with a computerised trading system.


**Lesson:** Small, quick losses keep you in the game. Once a trade moves in your favour, you can[trail your stop loss to break-even](https://algotest.in/blog/trail-stop-loss-to-break-even-price-when-backtesting/) so a winner doesn’t turn into a loser.


### 4. “If you lose all your chips, you can’t bet.”


**Source:** Larry Hite gave this as the second of his two basic rules in *Market Wizards* . The first is that if you don’t bet, you can’t win.


**Lesson:** Risk only a small share of your capital on each trade. A[run of losses](https://docs.algotest.in/backtest/monte-carlo-drawdown) can last longer than your past results suggest.


### 5. “You only find out who is swimming naked when the tide goes out.”


**Source:** Warren Buffett wrote this in his 2001 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders.


**Lesson:** Leverage and hidden risks look harmless in calm markets and only show up in a crash. Judge a strategy by its worst month, not its best.

## Trading Psychology Quotes


Most trading mistakes happen in the head before they happen on the screen.


### 6. “Anything can happen.”


**Source:** This is the first of the five fundamental truths in Mark Douglas’s *Trading in the Zone* (2000).


**Lesson:** Any single trade can lose, even one with a perfect setup. Douglas’s second truth explains why that’s fine: you don’t need to know what happens next to make money. You need an edge and a plan for when you’re wrong.


### 7. “Win or lose, everybody gets what they want out of the market.”


**Source:** Ed Seykota said this in *Market Wizards* , adding that some people seem to like to lose.


**Lesson:** If you keep breaking your own rules, ask what trading is really giving you: excitement, the feeling of being right, or profit. Only one of those pays.


### 8. “Be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful.”


**Source:** This line comes from Warren Buffett’s 1986 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders. It is usually quoted in this shorter form.


**Lesson:** Crowd fear often shows up in option prices as high[implied volatility](https://algotest.in/feature/ivr-ivp) . That’s when options are expensive, which matters whether you buy them or sell them.


Related:[18 Best Stock Market Movies and Web Series Every Trader Should Watch](https://algotest.in/blog/must-see-movies-for-finance-professionals/)


### 9. “A stock operator has to fight a lot of expensive enemies within himself.”


**Source:** This is from *Reminiscences of a Stock Operator* (1923), Edwin Lefèvre’s classic based on the career of Jesse Livermore.


**Lesson:** Hope, fear and greed cost real money. Writing your rules down before the market opens takes most of those decisions out of the heat of the moment.


### 10. “It never was my thinking that made the big money for me.”


**Source:** This is also from *Reminiscences of a Stock Operator* . The narrator goes on to say the big money came from sitting tight in winning trades.


**Lesson:** Many traders cut winners early and hold losers too long. Decide in advance how you will exit a winning trade, not just a losing one.

## Stock Market Quotes on How Markets Behave


### 11. “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.”


**Source:** Warren Buffett used this line in his 2008 shareholder letter and credited it to his teacher, Benjamin Graham.


**Lesson:** A cheap option isn’t automatically a good trade. A far out-of-the-money option costs little because it rarely pays off.


### 12. “Invest at the point of maximum pessimism.”


**Source:** This is Sir John Templeton, founder of the Templeton Growth Fund.


**Lesson:** The best prices often appear when the news is worst. That isn’t a signal to buy blindly. It’s a reason to have your plan ready before the panic arrives.


### 13. “The trend is your friend except at the end where it bends.”


**Source:** Ed Seykota, as quoted in Jack Schwager’s *Technical Analysis* (1995).


**Lesson:** Trend rules work until the trend changes, so every trend strategy needs an exit rule. You can test a trend rule built on a[moving average or ADX](https://algotest.in/feature/signals/indicators?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=indicators&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=indicators) against past data before you trust it.


## 2 Famous Market Quotes Usually Credited to the Wrong Person


### 14. “The market can remain irrational longer than you can remain solvent.”


**Source:** This line is almost always credited to John Maynard Keynes, but there is no solid record that he said it. The earliest known uses come from the financial analyst A. Gary Shilling in the 1980s.


**Lesson:** Being right too early can still wipe you out, especially on leveraged positions where[margin](https://algotest.in/margin-calculator) needs can rise against you.


### 15. “The stock market is a voting machine rather than a weighing machine.”


**Source:** This is what Benjamin Graham and David Dodd actually wrote in *Security Analysis* (1934). The popular version adds that the market becomes a weighing machine in the long run. That version comes from Warren Buffett, who credited Graham with it in his 1987 letter.


**Lesson:** Short-term prices reflect mood, while long-term prices tend to follow fundamentals. Intraday and expiry-day traders live in the “voting” phase, so they need rules, not opinions about fair value.


Quotes Every Systematic Trader Should Remember


### 16. “If you use sufficiently rigorous methods to avoid hindsight, you can test a system.”


**Source:** Larry Hite said this in *Market Wizards* . He added that such testing gives a fairly good idea of how a system will perform.


**Lesson:** A fair[backtest](https://algotest.in/feature/backtest) uses only the information available at the time of each trade, plus realistic costs. That is the difference between testing a strategy and fitting it to the past.


### 17. “All models are wrong, but some are useful.”


**Source:** This is the statistician George Box.


**Lesson:** No backtest matches live trading exactly, because of slippage, costs and timing. Expect some gap between[backtest and live results](https://algotest.in/blog/why-is-there-is-difference-between-my-live-trade-vs-forward-test-vs-backtest-results/) , and judge a strategy by whether it is still useful after that gap.


### 18. “You must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.”


**Source:** The physicist Richard Feynman said this in his 1974 commencement speech at Caltech.


**Lesson:** If you keep tweaking settings until a backtest looks perfect, you have fooled yourself. Check the strategy on fresh data with[paper trading](https://algotest.in/blog/paper-trading-for-beginners/) before you risk money.


## Share Market Quotes From Indian Investors


### 19. “Respect the market. Have an open mind. Know what to stake.”


**Source:** Rakesh Jhunjhunwala often said this, according to the book *The Big Bull of Dalal Street* . He would also add that you must know when to take a loss.


**Lesson:** Decide your stake before the trade, and decide in advance when you will accept you are wrong.


### 20. “The biggest quest to learn anything is curiosity.”


**Source:** Rakesh Jhunjhunwala said this in an interview published in February 2019. In the same interview he said markets have to be learnt through hands-on experience.


**Lesson:** Read[trading books](https://algotest.in/blog/best-books-on-options-trading-india/) , but learn by doing: test ideas, review the results and keep asking why.


### 21. “Small in size, medium in experience, large in aspiration, extra-large in market potential.”


**Source:** This is Vijay Kedia’s SMILE rule for picking stocks.


**Lesson:** A simple checklist beats gut feel. Kedia uses his to pick companies, and you can build one for your trades the same way.

### From Sticky Note to Strategy


A quote on your desk only helps if it changes what you do. Pick one from this list and write it as a rule:


-


Seykota’s advice on cutting losses becomes a fixed stop loss on every trade.


-


Hite’s rule about chips becomes a cap on how much capital any one trade can risk.


-


Buffett’s line on fear and greed becomes a check on implied volatility before you buy or sell options.


Add your entry and exit, then see how the rule holds up in both calm and volatile markets.

### FAQs


#### What is the most famous trading quote?


Buffett’s line about being fearful when others are greedy is probably the most quoted overall. Among traders, Paul Tudor Jones’s “play great defense” and Ed Seykota’s “cutting losses” come up most often.


#### What are good stock market quotes for beginners?


Start with Buffett’s “never lose money” rule, Larry Hite’s line about losing all your chips, and Mark Douglas’s “anything can happen”. All three teach that protecting your capital comes before making money.


#### Did Keynes really say the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent?


There is no solid record that he did. The earliest known uses come from the analyst A. Gary Shilling in the 1980s. Keynes was credited with the line years after his death.


#### Which trading psychology quote is the most useful?


Mark Douglas’s “Anything can happen” is a strong pick. Once you accept that any single trade can lose, it becomes easier to take small losses and stick to your plan.


#### Can trading quotes make you a better trader?


Only if you turn them into rules and test those rules. A quote can change how you think, but your results change only when your process does.
